steps.detail: The FTC is not calling to deactivate your phone number: problems: Channel mismatch: the source describes this scheme as a phone call ("calls to say a phone was registered under your name"; the fake official "reads off their badge ID"), but the scamName, title ("Fake government agent text says your phone will be cut off") and the on-screen message present it as a text message. The recreated provenance covers the wording, but the title tells viewers this scam arrives by text, which the source does not say. Reframe it as a call, or say the call version was adapted into a text. (rewrite 1 of 2)

The FTC is not calling to deactivate your phone number: problems: The recreated message never claims to be from the FTC. The sender and body say "Consumer Protection Office," but the stamp ("The FTC won't cut you off") and the secrecy flag ("A real FTC employee never...") rely on the FTC rules from the source. Viewers could wrongly think these red flags only apply when the FTC is named. The FTC's statements also say nothing about what a generic "Consumer Protection Office" would or would not do. The message should name the FTC, as in the source (e.g., "FTC official"), or the spoken lines should be reworded to match the sender. (rewrite 2 of 2)
The FTC is not calling to deactivate your phone number: both reviews agree: scam, no problems
